title: Vantage Point
events_chronological: Spanish police and the American Secret Service seal off the Plaza Mayor in Salamanca for a counter-terrorism summit.
In a television truck at the edge of the square, producer Rex Brooks directs the live coverage and argues with her crew over the shots.
Secret Service agent Thomas Barnes, back on duty after taking a bullet for the President, works the crowd with his partner Kent Taylor.
Local policeman Enrique is drawn away from his post by his girlfriend Veronica, who is part of the plot without his knowing it.
American tourist Howard Lewis films the plaza on his camcorder and catches faces nobody else notices.
A double stands in for President Ashton on the podium and is shot twice by a sniper.
Two bombs go off, one in the crowd and one under the podium, killing dozens.
Barnes sees Enrique running from the square and chases him through the streets, convinced he is a bomber.
Kent Taylor, secretly part of the plot, is exposed and shot dead by his own conspirators.
The mastermind Suarez and his team take the real President out of a hotel safe room and drive him away in an ambulance.
Barnes gets hold of Howard's camcorder and identifies the conspirators on the footage.
Veronica learns that her brother Javier has been forced into the plot by a hostage held over him, and she is killed.
Barnes commandeers a car and chases the ambulance across the city.
Javier is ordered to detonate his vest and refuses once he sees that his brother is safe.
The ambulance swerves to avoid Howard, who has run into the road after a lost child, and crashes.
Suarez is shot dead, the President is pulled out of the wreck alive, and Barnes collapses from his injuries.
syuzhet_notes: The film replays the same twenty-three minutes eight times, rewinding to noon with an on-screen clock at the end of each pass and handing the point of view to a different witness. Told-order bullets 1-11 therefore circle one short span of time instead of moving through it, and every rewind puts the film back behind the point it had just reached. Only from told-order bullet 12 does the story finally run forward to its end.
fabula_notes: Because the passes overlap almost entirely, this chronology orders material the film presents as simultaneous or repeated; several bullets are visible in more than one pass and are counted once here. What the real President is doing during the plaza scenes is withheld until the fifth pass.
